    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Instruction-memory contents",
      "Unit": "neorv32_imem",
      "Information": "The application image or runtime instruction-memory words used to supply instructions and stored data to the processor. In ROM mode the contents come from the initialized image, while in RAM mode bus writes can replace selected words.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The memory contents can include proprietary code or data and are exposed through the read path from the ROM or RAM arrays to bus_rsp_o.data at lines 81, 95, 128-131, 159-162 and 185. In RAM mode, bus_req_i.data can modify the stored contents through the byte-memory assignments at lines 116-125 and 145-154. The memory is required for instruction service, and rden can suppress the returned word through lines 173, 176 and 185, while corrupted RAM contents can also prevent correct execution.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could issue memory reads to disclose application contents, perform byte-enabled writes to corrupt instructions or data, or prevent read responses so execution or required transfers fail.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"

        185
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "Memory read-response enable",
      "Unit": "neorv32_imem",
      "Information": "The registered read-enable state that determines whether the selected memory word is presented on bus_rsp_o.data. It has no entry or exit port carrying it because bus_req_i fields only decide this internal control and it only gates the response.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "no",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"

      "Rubric Reason": "The internal rden state gates bus_rsp_o.data at line 185 and can be cleared or loaded low by the reset and request logic at lines 173 and 176, withholding a required read response.",

      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The address only selects or indexes the memory word affected by an access at lines 101, 116-131 and 142-162, so it is a path to the memory contents rather than independently protected information, and addr_ff is only a transient address copy."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus access command fields",

      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_imem",

      "Why Not Kept": "bus_rsp_o.ack only acknowledges or qualifies the bus request at lines 174 and 178-180, while bus_rsp_o.err is tied to a constant at line 186, so neither is an independent information asset."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Build-time memory configuration",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_imem",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "IMEM_SIZE, IMEM_INIT and alt_style_c only select the build-time memory implementation at lines 24-25, 38 and 73-107, and cannot be changed or withheld by the IP at run time."

conceptual assets.rubric reason: The memory contents can include proprietary code or data and are exposed through the read path from the ROM or RAM arrays to bus_rsp_o.data at lines 81, 95, 128-131, 159-162 and 185. In RAM mode, bus_req_i.data can modify the stored contents through the byte-memory assignments at lines 116-125 and 145-154. The memory is required for instruction service, and rden can suppress the returned word through lines 173, 176 and 185, while corrupted RAM contents can also prevent correct execution.
